environment.description: Same Ktor microservice deployed behind Kong Gateway (OSS 3.6) with a custom request-validator plugin configured via declarative config (kong.yml). The plugin enforces a JSON Schema on POST /api/v1/encrypt that requires the 'context' field to match a strict pattern: it must be a UUIDv4 string (regex ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$). The schema also sets 'additionalProperties: false'. The Kong plugin operates in 'strict' mode where schema validation failures return 400 before proxying. Upstream callers are required to generate a fresh UUIDv4 for each encryption request via their SDK (client-side enforcement is NOT relied upon - the gateway rejects non-UUID context values). The combination of gateway-enforced unique context per request means the deterministic nonce derivation produces a unique nonce each time, preventing nonce reuse.

config.network: Kong is only ingress path, service has no direct exposure (NetworkPolicy denies all ingress except from kong-proxy pod)
config.rate_limiting: none explicitly, but schema forces unique context
